content: In Joel, what kind of insects ate up the land?
explanation: Swarm after swarm came. “What the devouring locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten” (Joel 1:4, BSB)

content: In Joel, God promises to pour out His Spirit on whom?
explanation: Peter quoted this at Pentecost. “And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people.” (Joel 2:28, BSB)

content: In Joel, who will be saved?
options: Everyone who calls on the LORD
explanation: Paul quoted this in Romans. “And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved” (Joel 2:32, BSB)

content: In Joel, what should you rend instead of your garments?
explanation: God wants true repentance. “So rend your hearts and not your garments” (Joel 2:13, BSB)

content: In Joel, how is God described when calling people to return?
explanation: He is slow to anger. “For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion.” (Joel 2:13, BSB)

content: In Joel, what does God promise to repay?
explanation: God restores what was lost. “I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts” (Joel 2:25, BSB)

content: In Joel, when the Spirit is poured out, what will young men see?
explanation: Old men will dream dreams. “your young men will see visions.” (Joel 2:28, BSB)

content: Who was the prophet Joel's father?
explanation: The word of the LORD came to Joel. “This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel” (Joel 1:1, BSB)

content: In Joel, where will there be deliverance?
explanation: Among the remnant called by the LORD. “for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance” (Joel 2:32, BSB)
